texts.title: Money matters… up to what point?
texts.hook.h1.frame: How much would make you happy?
texts.hook.h1: Try it: think of the salary that would make you happy… and remember it till the end.
texts.hook.h2.frame: Each raise… waiting for the next
texts.hook.h2: Every raise makes me happy for a month… then I wait for the next one.
texts.hook.h3.frame: Salary doubled… would your day change?
texts.hook.h3: If your salary doubled tomorrow… would your day be any better?
texts.hook.h4.frame: Raise just in… eyeing the next
texts.hook.h5.frame: Money matters… up to a number?
texts.hook.h5: A famous book says: money matters… up to a certain number. Right?
texts.s1.n1: This is Karim. He just got a raise.
texts.s1.l3: Well… when I get to the next number.
texts.s1.n2: Let's replay it… this time he won't wait for the next number.
texts.s1.l4: Nice… the rent will be easier.
texts.s1.l6: Yes. It won't fix everything… but it made a difference.
texts.book.card: Each extra bit of money matters less… until it hardly matters.
texts.book.l1: The book says: each raise matters less… until you hit a ceiling.
texts.verdict.card: Analysis of 86 studies · leaving poverty linked to the biggest difference · after that: a smaller difference in wellbeing, a much smaller one in mental health
texts.verdict.nuance: And money is linked more to your life satisfaction… than to your daily mood.
texts.verdict.l2: The first part is probably right: leaving poverty is linked to the biggest difference, and after that, a smaller one.
texts.verdict.l3: And the ceiling? Unclear: life satisfaction is linked to income, in Egypt too… and in America even above 120,000 dollars a year.
texts.takeaway.l1: Try it like Karim: don't put off your joy until the next number. It may help.
texts.share: Send this to someone waiting for the next number to be happy.
